question: What disease in adults means ‘soft bones’ that usually develops due to a deficiency of vitamin D (often from not getting enough sunlight), or less often, digestive or kidney disease?
solution:
The correct answer is** Osteomalacia.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Osteomalacia **is softening of the bones.
 
• It most often occurs because of a problem with** vitamin D**, which helps your body absorb calcium.
 
• The body needs calcium to maintain the **strength and hardness of bones.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Osteopenia** is when your bones are weaker than normal but not so far gone that they break easily, which is the** hallmark of osteoporosis.**
 
• Most cases of** Osteomyelitis **are caused by** staphylococcus bacteria,** types of germs commonly found on the skin or in the nose of even healthy individuals.
 
• A lifelong lack of calcium plays a role in the development of** Osteoporosis.**
